title: Maintaining Proper Drainage Pipe Slope
description: Proper drainage relies on gravity to transport liquids and suspended solids together through horizontal piping. If a drain line lacks sufficient pitch, flow velocity drops, causing heavy solids to settle out and form obstructions. Conversely, excessive slope can allow liquids to drain rapidly while leaving solid waste behind. Standard code guidelines typically require a uniform pitch, such as one-quarter inch per foot for smaller branch drains, adapted to local regulatory requirements. Maintenance involves checking pipe hangers regularly to prevent sagging, which creates low spots where standing water collects.
